questions.text:
QUESTION ONE: THE DOPPLER EFFECT

Martin and Kerryn are riding their jet skis on a lake. Martyn's jet ski is fitted with an air horn that emits a frequency of 1043 Hz. At one point, Kerryn stops and Martyn travels directly towards her at a speed of 27.3 m s⁻¹. The speed of sound in air is 343 m s⁻¹.

Calculate the frequency of the sound that Kerryn hears.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: States correct answer. Working: f' = f × v_w/(v_w − v_s) = 1043 × 343/(343 − 27.3) = 1043 × 343/315.7 = 1133.19 ≈ 1130 Hz.

questions.text: Explain why Kerryn hears a different frequency than that emitted by the jet ski's air horn.
questions.expectedAnswer: As the jet ski approaches Kerryn, the wave fronts bunch up in front, making the apparent...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: States ONE of: higher f, lower wavelength, speed of sound constant. Merit: Complete answer: higher f AND lower wavelength AND speed of sound constant.

questions.text:
Kerryn is floating very close to the path of Martyn's jet ski, while her friend Erin is watching from a bank on the edge of the lake. The diagram shows positions A, B, and C along Martyn's path, with Kerryn at position B and Erin offset from the path.

The graph shows the frequency of the sound heard by Kerryn and Erin as the jet ski travels from A to C.

Explain why the frequency that Kerryn hears is the same or different to that which Erin hears.
questions.expectedAnswer: At A, both hear ~1130 Hz (jet ski far away, approaching directly).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Explains A, B, or C section. Merit: Explains B OR the transition between sections. Excellence: Complete answer explaining all sections including how the component of velocity towards each observer changes with position.

questions.text:
An underwater microphone has been submerged in the lake to monitor noise pollution from jet ski engines. Martyn's jet ski engine makes a sound at 574.0 Hz. As the jet ski travels away from the underwater microphone at 27.3 m s⁻¹, the microphone measures a frequency of 563.6 Hz coming from the jet ski engine.

Calculate the velocity of sound in water.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies '+' in denominator (receding source) OR substitutes correctly. Merit: Provides calculation with minor error or insufficient working. Excellence: Correct answer. Working: f' = f × v_w/(v_w + v_s). 563.6 = 574.0 × v_w/(v_w + 27.3). 563.6(v_w + 27.3) = 574.0 × v_w. 563.6v_w + 15386.28 = 574.0v_w. 15386.28 = 10.4v_w. v_w = 1479.45 ≈ 1480 m s⁻¹.

questions.text:
QUESTION TWO: STANDING WAVES

The cello is a stringed instrument belonging to the violin family. The strings are supported at each end by a piece of wood called the bridge and the nut respectively. The length of the strings between the supported ends is 0.690 m. When the cello is played, the strings can vibrate in different harmonics.

Draw a diagram of the 4th harmonic. Label the nodes and antinodes.
questions.expectedAnswer: Diagram showing 4th harmonic on a string fixed at both ends: 4 antinodes, 5 nodes (including...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct diagram (4 'bumps') with nodes and antinodes labelled correctly.

questions.text:
Sometimes if the cello has been in storage, the tension in the strings will decrease, and the instrument will be out of tune. The strings will therefore play a frequency that is other than the desired frequency.

Use the equation below to explain how this could have caused the frequency to be higher or lower than the desired frequency.

v(wave on string) = √(tension / mass per unit length)

No calculations are required.
questions.expectedAnswer: As tension decreases, v decreases (from the equation).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: States ONE of: v decreased, frequency decreased. Merit: Correct answer with two points linked. Excellence: Complete answer: tension decreased → v decreased (from equation) → frequency decreased (since v = fλ and λ constant) → note is lower.

questions.text:
When a 0.690 m string is played, the first harmonic has a frequency of 147 Hz. A finger is then pressed onto the string, changing the length of the string to play a first harmonic with a frequency of 207 Hz.

Calculate the new length of the string when the second note of 207 Hz is played.

Assume that the tension in the string remains constant.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Calculates ONE of: λ = 1.38 m, v = 202.86 m s⁻¹. Correct v in string with incorrect wavelength. Correct L. Merit: Correct v in string OR correct method from incorrect 1st harmonic wavelength. Excellence: Calculates correct answer with working. Working: λ₁ = 2L = 2(0.690) = 1.38 m. v = fλ = 147 × 1.38 = 202.86 m s⁻¹. λ₂ = v/f₂ = 202.86/207 = 0.98 m. L₂ = λ₂/2 = 0.49 m.

questions.text:
Two strings that are next to each other can be played at the same time. When string 2 is played (without a finger being pressed on it), it produces a note with a frequency of 98.0 Hz. Strings 1 and 2 are played at the same time that a finger is pressed onto string 1, and the length of string 1 is gradually reduced until a beat is heard.

Explain why beats form.
questions.expectedAnswer: When the two strings produce similar frequencies, the waves move in and out of phase.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: States one of: constructive produces loud, destructive produces quiet; pulsating volume heard. Merit: Explains beat formation (in phase → constructive → loud, out of phase → destructive → quiet). Excellence: Complete answer.

questions.text: Explain what will be heard as the length of the string continues to be gradually reduced.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Beat will decrease (then increase). When f₁ = f₂ then no beat is heard. Merit: OR how the beat frequency will change. Excellence: Complete answer explaining the decrease, zero beat, and then increase as the string continues to shorten.

questions.text:
QUESTION THREE: INTERFERENCE PATTERNS

A laser shines green light onto a double slit, which has a slit separation of 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ m. Each slit then acts as a light source that is in phase, producing an interference pattern on a screen with fringes that are close together.

When the screen is 3.40 m from the slits, the distance from the central maxima to the 3rd order maxima is 4.20 × 10⁻² m.

Show that the laser has a wavelength of 515 nm.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct answer. Working: nλ = d sin θ. sin θ ≈ tan θ = x/L = 0.0420/3.40 = 0.012353. d = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ m. 3λ = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ × 0.012353. λ = 5.1471 × 10⁻⁷ m ≈ 515 nm. If approximation not used: θ = arctan(0.0420/3.40) = 0.7079°. 3λ = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ × sin(0.7079°). λ = 514.9 × 10⁻⁹ m ≈ 515 nm.

questions.text: Explain why the intensity of the light on the screen varies, as shown in the interference pattern image.
questions.expectedAnswer: When path difference is a whole number of wavelengths, waves are in phase (constructive...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Explains changing brightness in terms of path difference. Merit: Explains constructive (in phase, whole wavelength path difference) and destructive (out of phase, half wavelength). Excellence: Complete answer linking path difference to constructive/destructive interference and consequent superposition.

questions.text:
The double slit is replaced with a diffraction grating which has more closely-spaced slits.

Describe and explain the changes to the interference pattern observed on the screen.
questions.expectedAnswer: Maxima are further apart (smaller d means larger angle for same order).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identify brighter OR identify more well defined. Merit: Identify AND justify one of: more well defined, brighter, maxima further apart. Excellence: Complete answer — justify THREE of: more well defined, brighter, maxima further apart (all justified).

questions.text:
In another experiment, a green laser, of wavelength 515 nm, is shone through a different diffraction grating and 7 maxima are seen on the screen. The screen is 0.900 m wide and is 1.20 m from the diffraction grating.

Calculate the possible range of values for the slit separation of the diffraction grating.
questions.expectedAnswer: 4.40 × 10⁻⁶ m < d < 5.87 × 10⁻⁶ m (most likely d = 5.00 × 10⁻⁶, i.e. 200 lines/mm).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: States/calculates ONE of: n = 3, θ = 20.556°. Merit: Calculates d = 4.4002 × 10⁻⁶ m (n = 3) OR n = 3 OR recognises range and uses nλ = d sin θ. Excellence: Correct answer giving a correct upper and lower limit of d. Working: 7 maxima so 3 either side of central maxima. 3 ≤ n ≤ 4. tan θ = 0.45/1.20, θ = 20.556°. For n = 3: d = 3(515 × 10⁻⁹)/sin 20.556° = 4.4002 × 10⁻⁶ m. For n = 4: d = 4(515 × 10⁻⁹)/sin 20.556° = 5.8669 × 10⁻⁶ m. So 4.40 × 10⁻⁶ < d < 5.87 × 10⁻⁶.
